chapter_theme: The trident by weekday (வாரசூலம்): each day of the week has a direction in which the inauspicious trident stands, and a journey made with it behind or to the left brings no grief, while one made with it ahead or to the right brings trouble.

797.reading: Telling how the trident falls by weekday: on Monday and Saturday it is in the east, on Tuesday and Wednesday in the north, and on Sunday and Friday in the west.
797.nuance: சேய் (the red one) names Mars, so Tuesday, and பானு the sun, so Sunday. The rule is travel lore of the kind still printed in almanacs; the verse gives no reason for it.

798.reading: On Thursday it is in the south; if the trident is to the left or behind, there is no grief, but if it appears to the right or in front, trouble grows on trouble.
798.nuance: மிக்கது மேல்வினை மேன்மேல் விளையுமே could also be read as 'further deeds grow greater and greater', a good result; the contrast with துக்கமும் இல்லை favours the bad sense, as the rule is usually given.

links.note: The Naladiyar counts those who prattle astrology among the greatest fools, beside those who neglect their real task; Tirumular sets weekday omens inside a yoga tantra. Whether this is a true conflict depends on whether the Naladiyar's சோதிடம் includes such day lore or means endless study that displaces the work of release.
